newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk president leaves for Lithuania amid crisis.
newsitem.headline: Turk president leaves for Lithuania amid crisis.

text.p: Turkish President Suleyman Demirel departed for a four-day visit to the Baltic republics on Monday, leaving behind uncertainty over early elections sought by the Islamist-led government.
A spokesman said Demirel flew out of Ankara airport for the Lithuanian capital Vilnius at around 0930 (0630 GMT). He is later to visit Latvia and Estonia.
Demirel, a veteran politician, is set to play a key role in a bid by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan to hand over power to his coalition partner in the runup to planned polls.
Istanbul stocks shrugged off the possibility of early polls, rising 2.50 percent in early trade on Monday.

Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader, announced on Sunday he would step down in favour of conservative government ally Tansu Ciller within a month. Ciller would then head a caretaker government to go to elections, but no date has been set.

Turkish newspapers said on Monday Demirel may throw a spanner in the works of the planned transition. They said the president had told Ciller on Sunday night there was no fixed formula for a power transfer.

"The president told Mrs Ciller that a handover of the prime minister's duties is not acknowleged in the constitution and that no procedure for it exists," the Hurriyet daily quoted Demirel saying in a statement.
Erbakan must first give his resignation to Demirel, an avowed secularist, who should nominate the party leader with the most members of parliament to produce a feasible cabinet list.
Erbakan's Welfare Party is the largest grouping in parliament. Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz would in theory be next in line for the chance to put together a government.
The present coalition government, battered by anti-Islamist defections, lost its absolute majority last week and now has 275 deputies in the 550-seat chamber. Two seats are vacant.
